You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of the Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]", "FINAL" and "market context" framing

The Seller's covering note says the [STANDARD] clauses were "reviewed and cleared by both sides," that the positions were "settled at principal level," and that only [OPEN] items need review. These are the counterparty's own assertions. Nothing in our record confirms them, and no clause is actually marked [OPEN]. Accepting the framing would mean not reviewing the package at all. I have therefore reviewed every item on its merits.

The "market context" ranges are also unsupported advocacy. Even on the Seller's own figures, it has taken the most seller-friendly end of every range. **Action:** before the mark-up goes out, confirm with Wattlebridge's principals whether anything was in fact agreed at principal level. If so, check exactly what and at what level of detail.

The Disclosure Letter is notably more candid than the cover note. It confirms that the Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay assignment and incident investigation are all **unresolved**, and that the bonuses are **not in the funds flow**. The cover note's descriptions ("addressed," "adequate," "not material," "ordinary course") are not supported by the Seller's own disclosures.

---

## 1. Price and funds flow (highest priority)

The deal is debt-free/cash-free at AUD 24m. Several Company liabilities are being left inside the business while the Seller takes the full price.

| Item | Amount | Seller position | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility (DD-003) | ~AUD 3.2m | Release "following Completion" | Repay at Completion out of the price |
| Completion bonuses (DD-005) | AUD 420k plus on-costs | "Matter for the Seller", not in funds flow | Deduct as a Transaction Expense or Indebtedness |
| Ironquay SOW3 fees (DD-010) | AUD 180k open (unverified) | Not addressed | Treat as debt-like if payable; pay at Completion |
| Sandbar renewals (DD-008/011) | AUD 330k | "Ordinary course" | Investigate; possible debt-like or leakage item |

That is **about AUD 3.8m of identified debt and debt-like items before on-costs**, roughly 16% of the price.

**Riverlark.** A post-Completion release is unacceptable on a debt-free deal.
- The change-control clause (8.1) may put the facility into default the moment the shares transfer.
- Security would stay over the Company's assets in the meantime.
- Require a payoff letter, a deed of release, PPSR discharge (and ASIC charge documents if relevant) delivered **at Completion**, with the payoff paid directly to Riverlark from the price.
- Confirm there is no share mortgage over the Paperbark shares, as that would also go to title.

**Bonuses.** The Company is the employer, so the liability, and any PAYG withholding, superannuation, payroll tax and workers' comp on-costs, sits with the Company and therefore with us.
- Calling them "a matter for the Seller" means nothing unless the price is reduced.
- Require the gross amount plus all on-costs to be deducted from the price, or funded by the Seller and paid through payroll at Completion.
- Back this with a specific indemnity. Confirm the continued-employment conditions do not leave a tail liability after Completion.

---

## 2. Liability regime (cl. 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

**Cap (12.1), 20% / AUD 4.8m.** This is the top of the Seller's own range and is only modestly above the identified debt items alone. Push for a higher general cap; it can be traded against W&I cover if one is being used. More importantly, the cap must apply **only to general warranty claims**. It should not apply to title/capacity, tax, specific indemnities, leakage/price adjustment, covenant breaches, or fraud.

**Thresholds (12.2).**
- The AUD 250k basket (~1.04%) is structured as a **deductible** ("only the excess"). Seek a **tipping basket**, so that once the threshold is crossed the whole amount is recoverable, and ideally a lower threshold.
- On the AUD 25k de minimis: claims arising from the same or related facts should aggregate.
- Neither threshold should apply to fundamental, tax or indemnity claims.

**Time limits (12.3/13).** 18 months is acceptable for general warranties, at most. Reject the proposal that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." It reverses the proper default and could quietly catch indemnities and tax. Instead:
- Tax: the relevant statutory amendment/assessment period plus a buffer (commonly 5–7 years).
- Title/capacity: 6–7 years or the statutory limitation period.
- Specific indemnities: their own tailored periods.

**Fundamental warranties.** Reject applying the general caps and time limits to title and capacity "for administrative simplicity." If the Seller does not own or cannot sell the shares, we have bought nothing. These warranties should be:
- capped at 100% of the price;
- free of any basket or de minimis;
- subject to a long survival period.

**Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying "to all Claims of any nature" (9.3/12.8/20.5).** Require express carve-outs for:
- fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its agents;
- specific indemnities;
- tax;
- leakage and price adjustment;
- the Seller's covenants.

Under NSW law, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy clauses also interact with misleading or deceptive conduct claims under s 18 of the Australian Consumer Law. They may not fully exclude that liability, but we should not concede drafting that attempts to. NSW counsel should confirm the final wording.

---

## 3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers (DL 1.1–1.2).** This would effectively hollow out the warranties: any document anywhere in the data room qualifies every warranty. Push for:
- only **specific disclosures**, fairly made with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter;
- data room documents to count only where specifically referenced against the relevant warranty;
- public registers limited to searches actually conducted and identified, if accepted at all;
- **no general disclosure** against fundamental warranties, tax or specific indemnities.

**Stale disclosure date.** The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, more than six weeks before today. Require an updated data room index and bring-down information. Any supplementary disclosure against warranties repeated at Completion should not cure a breach without Buyer consent, and should give a walk-away right if material.

**Disclosure Letter cl. 1.4 ("no admission").** This is tolerable as a statement that the Seller admits nothing. It should not be read as diluting the factual content of the specific disclosures in cl. 2–10, which we will rely on.

**Buyer knowledge (8.3).** Reject this. It bars claims for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew **or could have discovered** from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge and it guts the warranty package. Preferred position: an express statement that Buyer knowledge does not limit claims. Fallback: limit it to the *actual* knowledge of named Wattlebridge deal-team individuals, of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.

---

## 4. Specific matters

**Bluefen (DD-002). Critical, about 30% of revenue.**
- "Reasonable endeavours" plus treating the condition as satisfied on delivery of *a* written consent is inadequate.
- The consent must be a **condition precedent** that is unconditional, or on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably. It must evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied and must not vary pricing or terms adversely.
- The CP should be waivable **only by the Buyer**, with a long-stop date and a walk right.
- Ideally, require best endeavours from the Seller and a pre-Completion covenant to keep the Buyer informed and involved in communications with Bluefen.
- If Bluefen terminates or adversely varies within an agreed period after Completion, consider a price adjustment or escrow.

**Ironquay IP (DD-004/DD-010).** The existing indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, is not adequate. Under clause 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials occurs only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. The real risk is that the Company does not own IP it uses, not merely an unpaid AUD 180k. Require:
- verification of the payment position, with the fee paid from the price at Completion if outstanding;
- a **confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a CP**;
- a specific indemnity covering loss from any failure to own the SOW3 materials, infringement claims, and the cost of re-development or licensing. It should sit outside the cap and thresholds and carry a longer survival period.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006).** Do not accept "preliminary, not expected to be material." About 1,240 personal-information records were sent to an unintended external recipient. Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), Part IIIC), an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days of becoming aware of it. That window may already have closed, so a missed assessment or notification is itself a risk. Require:
- the incident timeline, the investigation findings to date, and any forensic report;
- a pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment and make any required notifications, with Buyer consultation;
- a specific indemnity outside the cap and thresholds covering regulatory, remediation, notification and third-party claims;
- tightened privacy and data-security warranties, specifically disclosed against only this incident;
- consideration of an escrow or retention.

**Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011), 3 × AUD 110k.** Three related renewals at identical amounts that the Seller itself says should be "read together" raise a question of whether they were split to stay below an approval or conduct-of-business threshold. "Related" also needs clarifying: is Sandbar a Seller-related party? Require:
- copies of the renewals, their timing against the signing and locked-box dates, and their terms on termination and committed spend;
- confirmation of whether any were entered into after the conduct-of-business covenants applied;
- if they are Seller-related or outside ordinary course, treatment as leakage or a price deduction, or termination before Completion at the Seller's cost.

**Tax and IP "settled under the general regime."** Not agreed. We need:
- a standalone **tax indemnity/covenant** for pre-Completion tax, outside the cap and thresholds, with a statutory-period survival;
- IP warranties with a cap and survival appropriate to a SaaS business, where IP is core value. Consider treating them as quasi-fundamental.

**Title (DD-012).** The share register alone is not enough. Require:
- a fundamental title warranty that the shares are free of encumbrances, options and rights of pre-emption;
- reconciliation against ASIC records;
- delivery of share certificates, or lost-certificate indemnities;
- confirmation of no Riverlark or other security over the shares;
- any constitutional or shareholder-agreement pre-emption waivers.

**Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The Seller's characterisation (notification only; no change-of-control trigger) is plausible but untested. Have our team review both provisions directly. Ensure the lease notification is given in time, as a Seller covenant. For Mossvale, check for any deemed-assignment or change-of-control wording. If it is ambiguous, obtain a comfort letter.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

**Must-haves (deal-critical):**
1. Reject the "[STANDARD]/FINAL" framing. Confirm internally what, if anything, principals agreed.
2. Funds flow: deduct Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) and the bonuses (AUD 420k plus all on-costs) at Completion. Treat the Ironquay fee as debt-like if payable. Riverlark payoff letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion.
3. Bluefen consent as a Buyer-waivable CP, unconditional or on acceptable terms, with the clause 11.3 conditions evidenced and a walk right.
4. Fundamental (title/capacity) warranties capped at 100% of price, no thresholds, long survival.
5. Fraud carve-out from all limitations, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy provisions.
6. Delete constructive buyer knowledge (8.3). Replace with no-knowledge-limitation or actual knowledge of named individuals of fairly disclosed matters.
7. Specific disclosure only. No general data room or public-register disclosure, and none at all against fundamentals, tax or indemnities.

**Strongly recommended:**

8. Specific indemnities, outside the cap and thresholds, for: the DD-006 incident, Ironquay IP ownership, the bonuses and on-costs, and pre-Completion tax.
9. Ironquay confirmatory assignment as a CP.
10. Tipping basket; aggregation of related claims for de minimis.
11. Reverse the "limitations apply to all Claims" default. Set tailored survival periods for tax, title and indemnities.
12. Updated disclosure and data room bring-down; no cure of breaches by supplementary disclosure.
13. Escrow or retention sized to the Bluefen, incident and Ironquay exposures, or W&I insurance with Seller-funded specific indemnities for known risks, which W&I typically excludes.

**Negotiable, depending on overall package:**

14. Level of the general cap (20% is the ceiling of the Seller's range, not a floor for us).
15. Basket quantum.
16. Sandbar: depending on what diligence shows, treat as leakage or a price adjustment, or accept with a specific warranty.
17. Lease and Mossvale: accept the Seller's characterisation subject to our own review and a covenant to give notices.

**Information requests to send now:** the Bluefen consent status and correspondence; the Riverlark payoff figure; the bonus terms and on-cost calculation; Ironquay payment evidence; the DD-006 timeline and investigation report; the Sandbar contracts and approval history; ASIC extracts and share certificates; and an updated data room index.

*Please treat this as a working analysis for the deal team. Final positions on the ACL interaction, the NDB timing and the tax survival periods should be confirmed by NSW and tax counsel.*
=== END ADVICE ===
